newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June car sales slip, but brief recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Japan June car sales slip, but brief recovery seen.

text.p: Car sales slipped in Japan in June for the third successive month, but the pace of the slide eased, suggesting a recovery was likely this month, an industry body said on Tuesday.
Sales fell five percent from a year earlier to 419,059 units in June, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said.
"The rate of the (year-on-year) fall shrank in June against May and April. That's a good sign. Domestic sales may recover this month to the same level as last year," an association official said.
Sales in May fell 9.4 percent, which followed a drop of 12.7 percent in April after Japan's consumption tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
But any year-on-year sales rises this month or in August are likely to run out of gas in September, one analyst said.
That is because sales started to climb from last September in anticipation of the sales tax increase, said Seiji Sugiura, an analyst at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

Only four of the smaller vehicle makers -- Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd, Mazda Motor Corp and Suzuki Motor Corp -- saw a sales increase in June, mainly the result of strong demand for new models, while the effects of the higher sales tax continued bite into sales of the other carmakers.
But carmakers are hoping the fact that many Japanese companies pay bonuses in July will help sales.
"Dealers are planning sales campaigns every weekend (to take advantage of the bonuses) so sales may recover in July (against last year)," Sugiura said.
Carmakers also said they hoped the introduction of new models would help consumers forget the consumption tax increase.
"We hope our sales bounce back this month with the new models," a Nissan Motor Co Ltd spokeswoman said.
Nissan said it received 4,000 orders for its Laurel luxury sedan in the first week after its launch on June 23, a large part of the way towards its monthly sales target of 5,000 units.
"The negative impact of the sales tax increase is likely to fade. We are sure the undertone of the domestic market is turning up," a Toyota Motor Corp spokesman said.
A spokesman for Honda Motor Co Ltd said: "Our sales are now recovering gradually... Our recreational models and weekend sales campaign are expected to help boost sales in and after July."
Mazda's sales in June jumped a steep 27.9 percent to 25,431 units, mainly due to good demand for its Demio compact car, a Mazda spokesman said.
